newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures end down, but T-bonds off lows.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures end down, but T-bonds off lows.

text.p: U.S. debt futures closed lower, but June T-bonds found light short-covering after testing a significant support level in early trade.
"You have to appreciate that we aren't carrying through on the highest consumer confidence reading in 28 years," one bond futures floor analyst said.
June T-bonds fell to 108-17/32 on U.S. May consumer confidence, which rose to 127.1, its highest level in 28 years, versus average trade estimates for a rise to 118.1.
The 108-17/32 is a 50-day moving average, and a Fibonacci retracement level from June's rally off 8-1/2-month lows.
With their slip to 108-17/32, June T-bonds retraced 50-percent of their rally from 106-12/32 on April 11 to 110-22/32, the 2-1/2-month high, on May 13.
The 108-17/32 also represents the point where June initially rallied to on April 29 in reaction to the employment cost index (ECI), the floor analyst said.
"We were in an uptrend from the day ECI came out to a couple of days before FOMC," he said. "But now we are trading below the bullish trend and could trade below the ECI rally."
He and other traders said the rebound from 108-17/32 in light intraday trade made the near-term picture less gloomy.

However, they said a close above 108-30/32, which is needed to reverse the near-term downtrend, was unlikely ahead of this week's U.S. economic line-up that culminates with revised Gross Domestic Product (GDP) data on Friday.
On Wednesday at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT, U.S. April durable goods orders data will be released. Orders are forecast to rise 1.3 percent, compared to down 2.6 percent in March.
Traders said a wire-service story saying that the U.S. Federal Reserve is "less than thrilled" with the U.S. budget package briefly pushed down June bond futures around midday.
In addition, rumors that hedge funds were heavy sellers of cash Treasuries persisted in afternoon trade, floor sources said.
June T-bonds opened lower, immediately pushing through 109-00, which equates to about a 7.00-percent yield on the cash long bond, on heavy dealer selling.

"Obviously there is a lot of anticipation about fund selling, given all the talk about the hedge funds' performance in Thailand," another analyst said. "There is still the feeling they are liquidating Treasuries to raise cash."

He noted that total open interest in T-bond futures has fallen 94,352 since May 14, 1997 when it set an all-time high of 602,440. On Friday, total open interest fell 14,837 contracts to 508,088, solidifying ideas funds may be liquidating positions in the U.S. Treasury market.
"I wouldn't be surprised to see another decline (in open interest) today," he said.

At the end of pit trade, June T-bonds were off 15/32 at 108-23/32, December Eurodollars were off 0.045 at 93.68 and 10-year notes were off 09/32 at 106-27/32. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
